themes_detail.label: Bus Stop Shelter Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Bus stop shelter complaints have spiked to 3 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1100% increase (z-score: 6.35)—suggesting either rapid deterioration of shelters or a coordinated maintenance failure affecting multiple transit nodes in Bushwick.
evidence: 3 bus stop shelter complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Spike is the single largest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating sudden concentrated issue
No prior news coverage or community board discussion suggests this is genuinely emerging
reporting_angles: Ground-truth check: visit affected bus stops to document shelter conditions (broken glass, missing panels, lack of benches)
Interview MTA about recent maintenance schedule or service cuts in CD 304

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints nearly doubled last week to 74 complaints compared to a 36.8 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 101% increase (z-score: 4.55)—indicating a potential sanitation or rodent crisis affecting multiple properties or streets.
evidence: 74 unsanitary condition complaints last week vs. 36.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (101% increase, z-score: 4.55)
Unsanitary Condition is also a top 10 complaint type overall (517 complaints over 90 days), indicating chronic baseline problem now accelerating
Community Board has repeatedly requested 'Other capital budget request for DSNY' (Sanitation), suggesting long-standing friction with Department of Sanitation responsiveness
reporting_angles: Map the 74 complaints geographically—are they clustered in one neighborhood or dispersed? What types of properties are affected (residential, commercial, streets)?
Investigate DSNY pickup schedule and staffing levels in CD 304; interview sanitation workers about route changes or staffing shortages
Interview residents and business owners about rodents, trash accumulation, or biohazard conditions

themes_detail.label: Special Projects Inspections Surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK compared to 0.5 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 700% spike (z-score: 4.95)—suggesting either targeted enforcement action or a concentrated code violation cluster that has triggered intensive inspections.
evidence: 4 SPIT complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 4.95)
SPIT is a Department of Buildings enforcement unit, suggesting code violations (likely housing/safety related)
Coincides with 435 total DOB permits filed over 90 days (282 alterations), indicating active construction/renovation activity that may have triggered compliance sweeps
reporting_angles: Request DOB SPIT activity logs for CD 304 this week—what properties are under inspection and for what violations?
Cross-reference with DOB permit data: are inspections targeting permitted or unpermitted work?
Interview DOB spokesperson about whether this is routine or part of an enforcement campaign in Bushwick

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Matter Spike
themes_detail.summary: Non-Emergency Police complaints surged to 16 last week compared to a 5.8 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 178% increase (z-score: 4.5)—indicating either a crime or disorder incident cluster or increased resident reporting of street-level quality-of-life issues.
evidence: 16 Non-Emergency Police complaints last week vs. 5.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (178% increase, z-score: 4.5)
Correlated with spike in 'Drinking' complaints (4 THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 average, 300% increase), suggesting open-air substance use or street disorder as likely driver
Also correlated with 'Overgrown Tree/Branches' complaints (9 last week vs. 3.2 average, 177% increase), suggesting overall conditions deterioration
reporting_angles: Request NYPD Compstat data for CD 304 last week—what types of complaints triggered 311 reports? Which precincts?
Interview NYPD about whether patrols increased or complaints shifted to new hotspot areas
Connect with residents in highest-complaint blocks to understand perceived safety issues and quality-of-life concerns

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees & Street Decay
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints nearly tripled to 9 last week compared to 3.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 177% increase (z-score: 3.89)—combined with street condition complaints (512 total over 90 days), indicating broader neighborhood infrastructure deterioration.
evidence: 9 Overgrown Tree/Branch complaints last week vs. 3.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (177% increase, z-score: 3.89)
Street Condition complaints total 512 over 90 days (rank #9 in overall complaints), indicating chronic infrastructure maintenance gap
Community Board budget request for 'Evaluate a public location or property for green infrastructure' suggests ongoing debate about tree canopy and stormwater management priorities
reporting_angles: Request NYC Parks tree maintenance schedule for CD 304—are there staffing or budget constraints limiting pruning?
Photograph the worst offenders and map complaints geographically to identify whether issue is systemic or localized to specific blocks
Interview Parks Department about whether 2024 budget cuts or staffing shortages have impacted maintenance cycles
